description:
Resuming a checkpointed OSD campaign fails after any commit, rebuild, or relocation because the resumption identity hash covers provenance context that does not affect resumed results.

## Background

`OsdCampaign::config_hash()` hashes the full serialized campaign, including `provenance.runtime.git_revision` (the repository HEAD) and `binary_sha256` (the SHA-256 of the running executable, which embeds absolute build paths). A committed checkpoint is therefore resumable only from the original working-tree revision, on the original machine, at the original path, with the original build artifact intact. Both fields are legitimate provenance to record; neither affects the resumed numbers once seeds, cells, interval, schema, and the dependency source closure are fixed. This contradicts campaign-resumability, which promises durable committed evidence that continues across sessions.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A checkpoint written at one repository revision resumes at a later revision when seeds, cells, interval, schema version, and dependency source closure are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: A checkpoint resumes under a rebuilt or relocated campaign executable with unchanged source closure.
- [hard] REQ-03: Recorded provenance still captures git revision and binary digest for every contributing run; the resumed receipt preserves each run's own provenance.
- [hard] REQ-04: A genuine behavioral mismatch (changed seeds, cells, interval, schema, or source closure) still refuses the checkpoint with a distinct, explanatory error.
title: resumption hash conflates provenance context with campaign identity
